### 2026-10-29: I completely forgot to start a timelapse and I only recently got wakatime working so here I am:

**3.5h**

I completely forgot to start a timelapse and I only recently got wakatime working so here I am:

Here is a quick list of things I did in this session with details following:
- Setting up the base part of the code
- Adding hardware debouncing to the rotary encoder
- Updating PCB layout
- Getting updated PCB files and screenshots

**Code:**

I started with the basics of the code by declaring all my global variables that I think I will need along with all the libraries, with this, I also included any pin numbers as constants so I can reference them later. Finally I declared the screen here which took a little research and looking at the guide since this is my first time using a screen at all.

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 032954](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/oevoP7jO4uTvd60Ew3652grvpX7eA13X/af5e191ce622ae57e7d3924da327206819a1b72745cf405020c54989fe81389e.png)

After that I setup all my pins and included a couple lines to print an error message if no screen is found on the I2C address. I also made a simple title screen using the lopaka display editor which should show for a second after you turn it on:

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 032954](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/oevoP7jO4uTvd60Ew3652grvpX7eA13X/4b2772b5790caef9aca93757738b6c8b6267d925d4809d9ae7753af643c29998.png)

**PCB:**

After doing some research and reading a couple of datasheets I noticed that rotary encoders can have their contacts "bounce" when turning them, which can allegedly cause false detections and extra triggers. This didn't sound very fun to deal with for when I actually had my parts, so I decided to integrate a very basic filter into my PCB to overcome this (I could have also done this in the firmware but I wanted to make the coding as easy as possible).

Here is the change in the schematic with  the extra resistors and capacitors:

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 032954](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/oevoP7jO4uTvd60Ew3652grvpX7eA13X/bb0758f5dc2570386e8f1ca5568a27376a1d20f29cd8f0a33195c6633011624b.png)

After that all I had to do was update the board and re-export the manufacturing files.

Here is the updated board. The length had to be extended a bit to accommodate the extra passive components and I also ended up moving the JST connector for the battery more towards the left.

![Screenshot 2026-10-30 032954](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/oevoP7jO4uTvd60Ew3652grvpX7eA13X/dfa6f91b6ef41289eb03c9cee133f823ec238d1aac58bfdcebb26821a2f7b99d.png)

**What's next?:**

In the next sessions I really have to start focusing on the code since that is going to take the most time, and is also what I am most inexperienced in. However, I will be simulating it constantly with wokwi to make sure everything is in order.

But yeah, thats it from me so thank you for reading :)
